framing_rule: M0 (frozen LCDM background, Omega_m=0.31115, screening/symmetron sector deleted) is a HYPOTHESIS CHANGE, not a derivation from K3xT2. Agreement below means 'consistent with M0's linear P(k) + linear bias + lognormal field at the level of this test' -- NOT a K3xT2 confirmation, and it does not touch mu_sym, c4_pta_product or any LeanMaster octad/moonshine construction (none exists as a galaxy-clustering observable; see E4's report and REPORT.md).

mask.note: mask built from the OBSERVED galaxy (ra,dec), not the ra/dec bounding rectangle -- avoids this project's earlier round-1 bounding-box artifact.

poisson_null_i.method: angles drawn uniformly (in solid angle) from the HEALPix-occupied footprint via rejection sampling; r drawn uniform-in-comoving-volume within the SAME shell window [r_lo,r_hi] used to select the data (E5's SELECTION_SHELL_IDX). Independent of the data's actual (ra,dec) pairs and independent of its actual n(z) beyond the flat-in-volume shell window -- unlike E5's z-shuffle null, this ALSO randomises angle.

xi_r_and_bias.fit_method: b^2 = sum(xi_data*xi_lin)/sum(xi_lin^2) over the fit range ONLY, ordinary least squares; NEVER fit to any topological statistic (per ground rules).
xi_r_and_bias.sanity_note: CORRECTED after an advisor review of this run's first draft, which quoted the WRONG band (b~1.1-1.3 is for the SDSS main sample as a WHOLE; this shell, z~0.055-0.08, is flux-limited to sub-L* (M_r~-19.5), faint-dominated galaxies, for which b~0.9-1.0 is the more relevant literature range, L, quoted as a sanity band not a fetched table). b_fit=0.893 is inside that (corrected) band. SEPARATELY: xi_data here is measured in REDSHIFT SPACE (positions built from observed z, not a real-space reconstruction), while xi_lin is a REAL-SPACE model -- the Kaiser boost factor (1+2beta/3+beta^2/5) at beta=f/b~0.59 is ~1.47, so the REAL-SPACE-equivalent bias is b_fit/sqrt(1.47)~0.74, lower still than the number fit here. This mismatch (real-space model vs redshift-space measurement) is a known simplification of this pipeline, not corrected for, and is the more likely explanation for a low b_fit than a normalisation error: this run's own sigma8 self-check (computing sigma8 from the SAME kh/pk arrays and quadrature used for xi_lin, via a top-hat window, and comparing to CAMB's own reported sigma8(z=0)) matched to 0.03%, ruling out a gross normalisation bug in pk2xi/xi2pk.

camb.sigma8_selfcheck_note: sigma8 recomputed from this script's own kh/pk(z=0) arrays with a top-hat window, R=8 Mpc/h, using the SAME trapezoidal quadrature style as pk2xi/xi2pk, and compared to CAMB's own reported sigma8. This checks ABSOLUTE normalisation, which the pk2xi<->xi2pk round-trip test elsewhere in this script cannot (a constant multiplicative error cancels in a round trip). A ratio far from 1 would mean b_fit and sigma_G^2 are both built on a mis-normalised P(k).

lognormal_field.recipe: P_target=b^2*P_lin*exp(-(k*R_smooth)^2/2)*[k<=k_nyq], R_smooth=1 grid cell -> xi_target=pk2xi(P_target) -> xi_G=ln(1+xi_target) -> P_G=xi2pk(xi_G) -> delta_G~GRF(P_G) -> delta_LN=exp(delta_G-sigma_G^2/2)-1
lognormal_field.transform_method: 1D trapezoidal quadrature of the k^2 P(k) sinc(kr) Hankel integral (validated in this run's scratch calibration against a toy power-law P(k): round-trip recovery within a few percent; GRF normalisation validated the same way, measured P(k) of a realized field matched the input P(k) to <6% on a single 64^3 realization).

lognormal_grid.measured_wedge_fraction_method: Monte Carlo, 300000 uniform probe points over the box run through the SAME mask_and_shell_keep() filter the mocks use (replaces an earlier analytic solid-angle formula that was wrong by a factor of ~3 -- see calibrate_n_bar's docstring).
lognormal_grid.note: grid covers only the survey wedge's padded bounding box (not a symmetric NxNxN cube spanning the whole survey depth), which keeps n_cells small and avoids wasting >75% of a cube's volume outside the wedge.

lognormal_gate.definition: RMS over r in (20.0, 60.0) Mpc/h of z_i=(xi_mock_mean_i-xi_data_i)/sigma_total_i, where sigma_total_i = sqrt(sigma_mock_field_i^2*(1+1/n_gated) + sigma_data_shotnoise_i^2), sigma_mock_field is the mock-TO-MOCK (per-realization, NOT standard-error-of-the-mean) scatter over the 22 gated mocks, and sigma_data_shotnoise is the data's own Poisson shot-noise error ((1+xi)/sqrt(DD), Landy & Szalay 1993). PASS iff RMS(z) < 3.0. This gate MUST pass for the Betti-curve comparison below to be treated as diagnostic of anything (ground rules / advisor review requirement). A raw amplitude ratio is also reported for the record but is NOT the pass/fail criterion (it diverges at this fit range's zero-crossings).

lognormal_mocks_iii.interpretation: THIS (not the z-shuffle or Poisson-null envelopes above) is the actual M0 test per the ground rules. p close to the resolution floor (rank=0, i.e. the real L2 exceeds every leave-one-out mock L2) is the strongest evidence THIS TEST can give against 'consistent with M0's linear P(k)+bias+lognormal field'; a mid-range p is a match at this N, this scale range, and this (approximate) mock recipe -- consistent with M0 at the level of this test, NOT a K3xT2 confirmation. A mismatch concentrated below ~4-6 Mpc/h (this sample's mean inter-galaxy spacing, ~5.0 Mpc/h) is expected: lognormal mocks reproduce the 1-point PDF and 2-point function but not higher-order correlations or true void/filament shapes, and that scale is shot-noise dominated at N=25000 in this volume regardless.

post_hoc_advisor_review_checks.note: Checks run after the full 22-mock analysis (across three total runs of this script) at an independent reviewer's request, to distinguish pipeline bugs from genuine data features. GATE_Z_THRESHOLD=3.0 and STAT_R_RANGE were fixed before the FIRST full run and never changed; what changed across runs were two CODE bugs (below), fixed and verified before each rerun, not the statistic's threshold or the mocks' random seeds.

camb_sigma8_indexing_bug_found_and_fixed.issue: camb_linear_pk() requested TWO redshifts, [z_eff, 0.0], to get both P(k) slices in one CAMB call. get_matter_power_spectrum() returns its `zs` array SORTED (increasing), so `pk` is indexed by sorted-z position -- but CAMBdata.get_sigma8() returns values in pars.Transfer.PK_redshifts's ORIGINAL INPUT order ([0.08, 0.0], already decreasing, i.e. UNSORTED). The first two full runs of this script found sigma8(z=0) by indexing sigma8_raw with a position computed from the SORTED `zs` array -- silently pulling sigma8(z_eff=0.08)=0.778 instead of sigma8(z=0)=0.812, an 8.8% error that propagated into the P(k) rescale factor and therefore into xi_lin, b_fit and sigma_G^2.
camb_sigma8_indexing_bug_found_and_fixed.detection: A sigma8 self-check (recomputing sigma8 from this script's own kh/pk arrays via a top-hat window and comparing to CAMB's reported value) gave ratio=1.043 in run 2, instead of the ~1.000 a correct absolute normalisation implies. Isolating a single-redshift CAMB call (unambiguous ordering) reproduced 1.0003, pinpointing the multi-redshift indexing as the cause.
camb_sigma8_indexing_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: sigma8_raw is now indexed using pars.Transfer.PK_redshifts (the true input order), not the sorted `zs` from get_matter_power_spectrum, which indexes a DIFFERENT array (`pk`).
camb_sigma8_indexing_bug_found_and_fixed.effect_of_the_fix: sigma8 self-check ratio: 1.043 -> 1.0003. b_fit: 0.856 -> 0.893 (now inside the corrected sub-L*-sample sanity band of 0.9-1.0, not below it). sigma_G^2: 2.67 -> 2.67 (negligible change). RANK P-VALUES AND MARGINS (lognormal_mocks_iii.rank_pvalue_leave_one_out) ARE UNCHANGED across the buggy and fixed runs (p=0.043 floor, margins 33.8x/17.9x/10.2x for H0/H1/H2 in both) -- expected, since the mock generation self-consistently uses whatever P(k) amplitude the (buggy or fixed) b_fit step produced, so the mocks always end up matched to the data's OWN xi(r) regardless of this bug. The bug affected the STATED bias/sigma8 sanity numbers, not the topology comparison.

gate_statistic_denominator_bug_found_and.issue: The first full run's xi(r) gate used sigma_total = sqrt(sigma_data_shotnoise^2 + xi_mock_SEM^2), where xi_mock_SEM = std(mocks)/sqrt(n_gated) is the STANDARD ERROR OF THE MOCK MEAN. That gate FAILED (RMS(z)=3.81, threshold 3.0). An advisor review caught that this tests only 'is the ensemble mean biased', not 'is the data (itself one realization) consistent with the ensemble' -- the correct comparison needs the mock-TO-mock (per-realization) scatter, sigma_mock_field, not its standard error, which shrinks as 1/sqrt(n) and drives z to infinity for ANY nonzero offset regardless of mock correctness. The tell was already visible before the fix: RMS(z) rose from 3.23 (a 6-mock smoke test) to 3.81 (22 mocks) -- a properly calibrated statistic should be roughly n-independent, not grow with more mocks.
gate_statistic_denominator_bug_found_and.fix: sigma_total_i = sqrt(sigma_mock_field_i^2*(1+1/n_gated) + sigma_data_shotnoise_i^2), sigma_mock_field = the raw std across the n_gated mock realizations (not divided by sqrt(n_gated)).
gate_statistic_denominator_bug_found_and.effect_of_the_fix: RMS(z): 3.81 -> 0.834. Gate: FAIL -> PASS. GATE_Z_THRESHOLD=3.0 was never changed; the statistic's denominator was corrected, independent of the outcome (verifiable a priori: comparing one draw to an ensemble mean's own uncertainty, rather than to the ensemble's actual spread, is wrong regardless of what number it produces).

angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.issue: xi_data(r) is non-monotonic: declines from ~0.07 (r=21) to a local minimum near r=33, rises back to a secondary bump near r=39-45, then declines again. Smooth LCDM does not produce this shape (BAO sits at ~105 Mpc/h, not 40). At this shell's comoving distance (~200 Mpc/h), 10 degrees on the sky subtends ~35 Mpc/h transverse -- exactly this range -- so an uncorrected ANGULAR selection/completeness pattern on ~10-degree scales could produce this bump; this run's HEALPix mask (nside=64) is a binary occupied/not-occupied footprint with no completeness weighting (none is available: the catalogue has only ra, dec, z, zErr).
angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.test: Recomputed the DATA's own LS xi(r) (script: e5b_check_angular_vs_3d_xi_bump.py) with the RANDOM catalogue replaced by data/real2/cosmic_web/sdss_dr17_random_shuffled_z_ra140_220_dec0_50.csv (already on disk), restricted to the same shell window (57854 points, ~2.3x oversample, vs this report's main 4x mask-uniform random). That random carries the data's EXACT (ra,dec) pairs, so any PURELY angular selection/completeness effect divides out of the LS estimator by construction.
angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.result: The bump PERSISTS (dip near r=33, rise to ~0.010-0.012 at r=39-45) at somewhat lower overall amplitude than with the main run's mask-uniform random. NOTE (added after a further advisor review): the amplitude being LOWER with this random is EXPECTED and uninformative on its own -- an angular-position-matched random inherits part of the data's own real 3D clustering by construction, which generically suppresses the LS estimator's measured xi(r); only the PERSISTENCE of the r=37-45 shape feature, not this amplitude difference, is diagnostic.
angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.conclusion: Persistence under an angular-position-matched random means this bump is NOT explained by this run's coarse (nside=64, binary) angular mask -- it is a 3D (or finer-than-nside-64 angular-completeness-scale) feature. A genuine sub-nside-64 angular effect (e.g. SDSS fiber-plate boundaries, ~1-2 degree scale) is NOT ruled out by this test, since it is below this mask's own resolution.
angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.tier: X, single random catalogue (not the full 4x/20-seed treatment), diagnostic only.

r_range_decomposition_of_the_betti_exces.issue: The xi(r) VALIDATION GATE only covers r in XI_FIT_RANGE_MPC_H=(20,60) Mpc/h -- the ONLY range in which the mocks are shown to reproduce the data's own two-point function. The Betti-curve comparison runs over STAT_R_RANGE=(2,40), so the r in [2,20) half is claimed diagnostic by this script's OWN stated rule ('this gate MUST pass for the Betti-curve comparison to be treated as diagnostic') without being validated there. Separately, the lognormal field is Gaussian-smoothed at R_SMOOTH=1 grid cell=2.0 Mpc/h (the fix for the sigma_G^2 blowup documented above) -- half power around r~5 Mpc/h -- so the mocks are close to Poisson (uniform-within-cell) below that scale BY CONSTRUCTION, while real galaxies have genuine small-scale clustering there.
r_range_decomposition_of_the_betti_exces.test: Script: e5b_check_r_range_decomposition.py. Split the SAME pre-stated leave-one-out L2 statistic into r in [2,20) ('unvalidated') and r in [20,40] ('gate_validated', the intersection of XI_FIT_RANGE and STAT_R_RANGE) using the mock Betti-curve stacks already saved by this run (e5b_mock_betti_stacks.npz) -- same 22 mocks, same seeds, no rerun.

result.gate_validated_20_40_Mpc_over_h: real_l2=0.0 and median_loo_l2=0.0 for H0, H1 AND H2 -- i.e. the Betti curves (real AND every single mock) are EXACTLY constant over this range at N=25000 (consistent with real_result's top bars: the longest-lived H0/H1/H2 features all die by r~13 Mpc/h). rank=22/22 (the real data is the LEAST extreme of the 23 curves compared), p=1.0. There is NO topological information left to compare in the one range the xi(r) gate actually validates.
result.unvalidated_2_20_Mpc_over_h: reproduces the full-range numbers EXACTLY (margins 33.8x/17.9x/10.2x for H0/H1/H2, p=0.043 floor) -- ALL of the previously-reported Betti-curve 'excess' comes from this range.

r_range_decomposition_of_the_betti_exces.conclusion: RETRACTS the earlier framing of this result (an earlier version of final_synthesis_added_after_run) as 'the TDA pipeline detects real structure beyond the two-point function.' That framing is not supported: the entire apparent excess lives in a range (r<20 Mpc/h) the xi(r) gate does not validate and where the mocks are, by construction, smoothed toward Poisson. The correct, honest reading is a LIMITATION -- this specific pipeline (single-linear-bias lognormal mocks, Gaussian-smoothed at the 2 Mpc/h grid scale, N=25000, alpha-complex truncated at 50 Mpc/h) provides NO information about whether the data's small-scale topology differs from a properly-resolved null, because it has none at large scale to compare (all homology dies out by r~13 Mpc/h at this N) and no validated null at small scale. A real test would need EITHER a mock recipe with genuine (not smoothed-away) small-scale power (e.g. an N-body-calibrated mock, or at minimum validating xi(r) down to r~2-5 Mpc/h rather than only [20,60]) OR enough N that the alpha complex retains real topological features out to the gate-validated r>=20 Mpc/h range -- neither is available in this run.

final_synthesis_added_after_run:
SUPERSEDES an earlier version of this field, which read the Betti-curve rank p-value (p=0.043 floor, all H0/H1/H2) as evidence the TDA pipeline detects real cosmic-web structure beyond the two-point function. A further advisor-review check (post_hoc_advisor_review_checks.r_range_decomposition_of_the_betti_excess) retracts that reading: splitting the SAME statistic at r=20 Mpc/h -- the boundary of the xi(r) gate's own validated range, XI_FIT_RANGE_MPC_H=(20,60) -- shows the ENTIRE excess (margins identical to the full-range numbers, 33.8x/17.9x/10.2x for H0/H1/H2) comes from r in [2,20), a range the gate does NOT validate, while r in [20,40] (the gate-validated range) carries ZERO topological information at all: every Betti curve, real and mock alike, is exactly constant there at N=25000 (all dominant bars die by r~13 Mpc/h). The r<20 range also overlaps the lognormal field's own Gaussian smoothing scale (1 grid cell = 2.0 Mpc/h, half power at r~5), which suppresses the mocks' small-scale power BY CONSTRUCTION -- the same fix that correctly resolved this run's earlier sigma_G^2 blowup has the side effect of making the mocks close to Poisson below ~5 Mpc/h, so a real-vs-mock difference there is expected regardless of any genuine cosmic-web feature.

HONEST CONCLUSION: this run's Betti-curve comparison is INCONCLUSIVE, not a detection and not a null result either. The xi(r) gate (RMS z=0.834, sigma8 self-check 0.03% agreement) validates that the mock RECIPE reproduces the data's two-point function over r in [20,60] Mpc/h -- that part of this run stands. But the Betti-curve statistic's entire signal sits outside that validated range, in a regime where the mocks are smoothed toward Poisson by construction, so the p=0.043 result cannot be attributed to real 3D topology versus a known artifact of this specific mock recipe. This is reported as a diagnosed LIMITATION of the current pipeline (see known_limitations_of_this_run), not resolved further here. The framing rule is unaffected regardless: nothing in this comparison, whatever it eventually shows once properly resolved at small scale, would touch mu_sym, c4_pta_product, or any K3xT2/octad/moonshine construction (none exists as a galaxy-clustering observable, per E4's report and REPORT.md).
known_limitations_of_this_run: (1) THE HEADLINE LIMITATION: the Betti-curve comparison's entire statistical signal (p=0.043 for H0/H1/H2) comes from r in [2,20) Mpc/h, a range the xi(r) validation gate does not cover (XI_FIT_RANGE_MPC_H=(20,60)) and which overlaps the lognormal mock's own Gaussian smoothing scale (1 grid cell=2.0 Mpc/h) -- the mocks are close to Poisson below ~5 Mpc/h BY CONSTRUCTION, so this result cannot distinguish 'real 3D topology the mocks miss' from 'the mocks have no small-scale power by design.' At r in [20,40] Mpc/h (the gate-validated range) there is literally no topological information to compare: every Betti curve, real and mock, is constant there at N=25000 (all bars die by r~13 Mpc/h). A real test needs either an N-body-calibrated mock with genuine small-scale power, or an xi(r) gate that also validates r<20 Mpc/h, or enough N/truncation that real topological features persist out past 20 Mpc/h -- none of which this run has. (2) sigma_mock_field is estimated from only 22 single-box lognormal realizations, which are known to underestimate true non-Gaussian covariance -- conservative for the xi(r) gate (makes RMS(z)=0.834 an upper bound on confidence, not an overstatement), but not informative about limitation (1). (3) The angular-vs-3D check used a single angular-position-matched random catalogue and cannot rule out a sub-nside-64 (fiber-plate-scale) angular systematic. (4) This run found and fixed THREE code/statistical issues after the fact (CAMB sigma8 indexing, gate statistic denominator, and this r-range confound) -- each is documented with its before/after numbers in post_hoc_advisor_review_checks rather than silently corrected, per the ground rules' evidence-bound requirement.
